2. title: Runtime prefetching
3. description: Extend the App Shell with personalized content using the prefetch segment config and per-session caching directives.
4. nav_title: Runtime prefetching
5. version: experimental
6. related:
7.   title: Learn more
8.   description: Validate your structure and dive into caching primitives.
9.   links:
10.     - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
11.     - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
12.     - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
13.     - app/getting-started/caching
14.     - app/guides/instant-navigation
15. ---
16. 
17. The router prefetches an [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route as visible `<Link>` components enter the viewport. Runtime prefetching lets the prefetch also include content that depends on the request: cookies, headers, `searchParams`, and `params` not resolved by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params). On a direct visit, the `<Suspense>` boundaries around runtime data render their fallbacks and the content streams in. Uncached reads stay behind their fallback boundaries either way.
18. 
19. This guide assumes you've structured your route for instant navigation. If you haven't, start with the [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) to validate the route's caching structure first. Runtime prefetching costs a per-link server invocation. It only pays off when there's content past the App Shell worth resolving before the click.
20. 
21. ## What runtime prefetching does
22. 
23. A user on `/` sees a [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) to `/courses`. The destination mixes four kinds of content: a static heading, an `<EnrolledBadge>` that reads the session cookie, a cached `<FeaturedCourses>` list, and a `<LiveEnrollment>` count that has to be fresh on every request.
24. 
25. ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
26. import Link from 'next/link'
27. 
28. export default function RootLayout({ children }: LayoutProps<'/'>) {
29.   return (
30.     <html>
31.       <body>
32.         <nav>
33.           <Link href="/courses">Courses</Link>
34.         </nav>
35.         {children}
36.       </body>
37.     </html>
38.   )
39. }
40. ```
41. 
42. ```tsx filename="app/courses/page.tsx"
43. import { Suspense } from 'react'
44. 
45. export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'
46. 
47. export default function CoursesPage() {
48.   return (
49.     <>
50.       <h1>Courses</h1>
51.       <Suspense fallback={<BadgeFallback />}>
52.         <EnrolledBadge /> {/* reads the session cookie */}
53.       </Suspense>
54.       <FeaturedCourses /> {/* 'use cache' */}
55.       <Suspense fallback={<Loading />}>
56.         <LiveEnrollment /> {/* uncached, fresh per request */}
57.       </Suspense>
58.     </>
59.   )
60. }
61. ```
62. 
63. Without `prefetch = 'allow-runtime'`, the App Shell renders `<h1>` and `<FeaturedCourses>` directly, while the two `<Suspense>` boundaries show their fallbacks. After the click, `<EnrolledBadge>` and `<LiveEnrollment>` stream in.
64. 
65. When [`prefetch = 'allow-runtime'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is set on the route, the router prefetches a prerender of `/courses` that includes request data, beyond what's in the App Shell. `<EnrolledBadge>` resolves because the session cookie is available at prefetch time. `<LiveEnrollment>` still sits behind its fallback because no prerender can know its current value. After the click, only `<LiveEnrollment>` streams in.
66. 
67. The prerender advances through anything that's static or cached, then stops at uncached reads and falls back to the surrounding `<Suspense>` boundary. The boundary is already in place from your **instant-nav validation**.
68. 
69. The result is a **runtime prerender**: more of the page is already rendered before the user clicks, with fewer loading spinners.
70. 
71. Generating the runtime prerender costs **a server invocation per prefetchable link**, so it is opt-in per route.
72. 
73. > **Good to know:** A cold cache (first visit, or after expiration) means the server still has to compute the cached result. Users may see a loading spinner on that first navigation. Subsequent navigations are instant as long as the cache is warm.
74. 
75. ## Example: a dashboard layout
76. 
77. Take a dashboard layout with a nav that depends on request data. Without runtime prefetching, `<UserNav>` always streams in behind a `<Suspense>` fallback after navigation, even though the cookie that determines its content is already known when the prefetch fires. With runtime prefetching, the router prefetches a prerender that resolves `<UserNav>` before the click:
78. 
79. ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
80. export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'
81. ```
82. 
83. The route still needs a valid prerender, so `<UserNav>` stays behind a `<Suspense>` boundary:
84. 
85. ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
86. import { Suspense } from 'react'
87. 
88. export default function DashboardLayout({
89.   children,
90. }: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) {
91.   return (
92.     <div>
93.       <Suspense fallback={<nav>Loading...</nav>}>
94.         <UserNav />
95.       </Suspense>
96.       <main>{children}</main>
97.     </div>
98.   )
99. }
100. ```
101. 
102. `<UserNav>` reads a cookie, then looks up data based on it. The challenge is that `"use cache"` can't read `cookies()` inside the cached function. Two patterns handle this: **extract and pass** when the lookup result is shared across many users, and `"use cache: private"` when it's tied to a specific user.
103. 
104. ### Extract and pass
105. 
106. Read the cookie outside the cached function and pass the value in as an argument. `cookies()` stays outside the cache scope, the argument crosses the boundary, and the cached function has a deterministic signature. The cache entry is keyed on that argument; if many users share the value, they share the entry.
107. 
108. ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/user-nav.tsx"
109. import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
110. 
111. async function UserNav() {
112.   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
113.   const topics = await getTopics(team)
114.   return (
115.     <nav>
116.       {topics.map((topic) => (
117.         <a key={topic.id} href={topic.href}>
118.           {topic.label}
119.         </a>
120.       ))}
121.     </nav>
122.   )
123. }
124. 
125. async function getTopics(team: string | undefined) {
126.   'use cache'
127.   return db.topics.forTeam(team)
128. }
129. ```
130. 
131. On a direct visit, `<UserNav>` streams in behind the fallback. With runtime prefetching, the prerender resolves `<UserNav>` before the click because the team cookie is available at prefetch time. Users on the same team share the cache entry, so traffic to the underlying data scales with team count, not user count.
132. 
133. Anything without a caching directive still streams in after navigation. The runtime prerender is not a full server render. It advances only as far as the caching structure allows.
134. 
135. ### `"use cache: private"`
136. 
137. When the lookup is tied to a specific user, use [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). It assigns a cache lifetime to a function that reads cookies, headers, or other runtime data directly. Results are cached in the browser only, so the cache is per-user by definition.
138. 
139. ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/user-nav.tsx"
140. import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
141. 
142. async function UserNav() {
143.   const user = await getUser()
144.   return <nav>{user.name}</nav>
145. }
146. 
147. async function getUser() {
148.   'use cache: private'
149.   const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
150.   return db.users.findBySession(session)
151. }
152. ```
153. 
154. `cookies()` lives inside the cached function, which only works under `"use cache: private"`. This is also the pattern when you can't extract the runtime data from the outside: auth helpers that check `Date.now()` against a token's expiry, or session helpers that read cookies deep inside their own code, can't be wrapped at the call site.
155. 
156. Everything inside the scope shares the same lifetime, so colocate `"use cache: private"` as close to the runtime data access as possible.
157. 
158. ## When to reach for runtime prefetching
159. 
160. Use it on routes where:
161. 
162. - A useful chunk of the page depends on request data: cookies, headers, the full URL, `searchParams`, or `params` not resolved by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)
163. - That chunk has a known cache lifetime (it can be expressed with `"use cache"` or `"use cache: private"`)
164. - The traffic justifies the per-link server invocation
165. 
166. Skip it when the prefetch can't produce a better UI than the App Shell. Each visible `<Link>` to a route with `'allow-runtime'` wakes a server, and that cost only pays off if more of the page is ready before the click:
167. 
168. - The route has little or no runtime-data dependency. The App Shell already gets you instant.
169. - The dependent content has to be fresh on every request. The prerender stops at the same `<Suspense>` fallback, so the user sees the same UI either way.
170. - The route is rarely navigated to. You pay per visible link, regardless of click-through.
171. 
172. ## App Shells
173. 
174. A per-link runtime prefetch only helps the navigations where it fires before the click and completes before the click. On a slow connection, on a feed of many links, or on a direct visit, the per-link prefetch may not yet exist when the user navigates. Without something to fall back on, the navigation blocks until the server responds.
175. 
176. The [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) closes that gap. It's a per-route prerender, deduped across every link to the same route, generated and prefetched once per route rather than once per visible link.
177. 
178. App Shells are on by default with Cache Components. Pairing with `partialPrefetching: true` makes them the prefetch baseline for every route:
179. 
180. ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
181. import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
182. 
183. const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
184.   cacheComponents: true,
185.   partialPrefetching: true,
186. }
187. 
188. export default nextConfig
189. ```
190. 
191. N links to the same route share one prefetched App Shell, so rendering a `<Link>` is effectively free. To prefetch more than the shell (including request data like cookies, headers, params, and `searchParams`), opt the destination into [`prefetch = 'allow-runtime'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#allow-runtime) and use `<Link prefetch={true}>` on the link side.
192. 
193. > **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this, and the shell is cached per session on the client, not shared across users.
194. 
195. App Shells vs runtime prefetches:
196. 
197. |         | App Shell                                    | Per-link runtime prefetch (`allow-runtime`) |
198. | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
199. | Scope   | One per route                                | One per visible `<Link prefetch={true}>`    |
200. | Content | Route's rendered output minus per-link data  | Same, plus request data resolved            |
201. | Cost    | Bounded by route count                       | Bounded by visible-link count               |
202. | Role    | Every Cache Components route's instant floor | Upgrade: more rendered before click         |
203. 
204. ## Next steps
205. 
206. - [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for how `<Link>` behaves under the new model and how to migrate existing apps.
207. - [`prefetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) for all prefetch modes.
208. - [`use cache: private` reference](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) for per-user caching specifics.
209. - [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for validating the route's caching structure.
210. - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering.
211.
````

1. ---
2. title: instant
3. description: API reference for the instant route segment config.
4. version: draft
5. related:
6.   title: Next Steps
7.   description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice.
8.   links:
9.     - app/guides/instant-navigation
10.     - app/getting-started/caching
11.     - app/getting-started/revalidating
12.     - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
13. ---
14. 
15. The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.
16. 
17. Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.
18. 
19. When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.
20. 
21. > **Good to know**:
22. >
23. > - The `instant` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
24. > - `instant` cannot be used in Client Components. It will throw an error.
25. > - Next.js does not perform prefetches in development, so navigations may not feel as instant as they will in production. Validation reflects what will happen during `next start`, where prefetching is enabled.
26. 
27. ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
28. export const instant = true
29. 
30. export default function Page() {
31.   return <div>...</div>
32. }
33. ```
34. 
35. ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
36. export const instant = true
37. 
38. export default function Page() {
39.   return <div>...</div>
40. }
41. ```
42. 
43. ## Reference
44. 
45. The export accepts:
46. 
47. - **`true`**: Opts the segment into validation at whatever level is configured globally (see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults)). With the framework defaults, validation runs in development only and surfaces errors in the dev overlay.
48. - **`false`**: Opts the segment out (see [Disabling instant](#disabling-instant)).
49. - An **object**: Opts in with additional options. See [`level`](#level).
50. 
51. ### `level`
52. 
53. Sets the severity at which validation runs for this segment.
54. 
55. ```tsx filename="page.tsx"
56. export const instant = {
57.   level: 'warning',
58. }
59. ```
60. 
61. - **`'warning'`**: Validates in development only. Errors appear in the dev overlay; the build is unaffected.
62. 
63. In the future a validation level that supports validation during build will be supported. Unless you are enabling experimental validation modes there is no need to specify level since the only level available is `"warning"`.
64. 
65. When `level` is omitted (or `instant = true` is used), the segment is validated at whatever level is configured globally — see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults).
66. 
67. ### Disabling instant
68. 
69. Set `false` on a layout or page to indicate that this segment is allowed to block when navigating to it.
70. 
71. This is useful when a deeper page should be instant but an ancestor can't be. For instance, if a shared layout cannot load instantly but you still want to assert that pages beneath this layout can be navigated to instantly, you can ensure that the pages have `instant = true` while the shared layout has `instant = false`.
72. 
73. ```tsx filename="app/tabs/layout.tsx"
74. export const instant = false
75. ```
76. 
77. ```tsx filename="app/tabs/[tab]/page.tsx"
78. export const instant = true
79. ```
80. 
81. Navigations from outside into a tab are allowed to block at the layout. Navigations between tabs are validated for instant UI.
82. 
83. You don't need to add `false` to ancestors of an instant page just because they do something blocking — a higher-up `instant = true` doesn't force its descendants to validate, and leaving an ancestor unconfigured is fine. Reach for `false` only when you've configured a deeper page as instant and need to exempt navigations that pass through a blocking ancestor.
84. 
85. ### Disabling static shell validation
86. 
87. Cache Components also validates that each page in your app produces a non-empty static shell at prerender time. To opt a route out of this validation, ensure the highest `instant` config in the route's tree is `false` — a `false` higher in the tree takes precedence over any deeper `true` for the static-shell check.
88. 
89. Setting `false` on the root layout disables static shell validation for the entire app. Place the `false` as low as possible — only as high as needed to cover the routes you want to opt out — so the rest of the app keeps validating.
90. 
91. ## How validation works
92. 
93. `instant` triggers validation at every shared layout boundary in the route. Validation runs during development (on page loads and HMR updates) and surfaces errors in the dev error overlay.
94. 
95. Each error identifies the component that would block navigation. The fix is usually to cache the data with `use cache` or wrap it in a `<Suspense>` boundary.
96. 
97. ## Configuring validation defaults
98. 
99. By default (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. The `experimental.instantInsights.validationLevel` config tunes this behavior — for example, to limit validation to segments that opt in explicitly via `instant`.
100. 
101. ```js filename="next.config.js"
102. module.exports = {
103.   experimental: {
104.     instantInsights: {
105.       validationLevel: 'warning',
106.     },
107.   },
108. }
109. ```
110. 
111. The supported levels are:
112. 
113. - **`'warning'`** _(framework default)_: Every Page and Default segment is implicitly validated at warning level (dev only).
114. - **`'manual-warning'`**: Only segments with an explicit `instant` are validated, at warning level (dev only).
115. 
116. Setting `instant = false` on a segment opts it out of validation entirely.
117. 
118. > **Good to know**:
119. >
120. > - The framework default may change in future versions to opt users into higher levels of validation. Because this feature is experimental, that change is not considered a breaking change. To pin a specific behavior, set `validationLevel` explicitly.
121. > - Framework-synthesized error routes (`/_global-error`, `/_not-found`) are excluded from implicit validation. To validate them, opt in explicitly with `instant`.
122. 
123. ## Inspecting loading states
124. 
125. The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled:
126. 
127. ```js filename="next.config.js"
128. module.exports = {
129.   cacheComponents: true,
130. }
131. ```
132. 
133. Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then click **Start Capturing**. While capturing is active:
134. 
135. - Refresh the page to freeze the initial static UI generated for the route, before any dynamic data streams in.
136. - Click a link to freeze the prefetched UI for the destination route.
137. 
138. When the UI is frozen, click **Continue Rendering** to let the current navigation finish while keeping the Navigation Inspector in capturing mode. Click **Stop Capturing** when you are done. Use both page refreshes and link clicks to check that your loading states look right on first visit and on navigation.
139. 
140. ## Testing instant navigation
141. 
142. The `@next/playwright` package exports an `instant()` helper that holds back dynamic content while the callback runs against the instant UI. See the [guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for a full example.
143. 
144. ```typescript
145. import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
146. ```
147. 
148. {/* TODO: remove when fixed and from prod-docs-release */}
149. 
150. ## Known issue: shared cookie across projects
151. 
152. The DevTools use a `next-instant-navigation-testing` cookie to hold back dynamic content and freeze the page at the instant UI. Because cookies are scoped to the domain and not the port, running multiple projects on the same domain (typically `localhost`) means the cookie is shared across them and can cause unexpected behavior. Clear the cookie or close the Navigation Inspector panel when switching between projects to avoid issues.
153. 
154. > **Good to know:** This will be fixed as part of stabilizing the feature.
155. 
156. ## TypeScript
157. 
158. ```tsx
159. type InstantConfig =
160.   | true
161.   | false
162.   | {
163.       level?: 'warning'
164.     }
165. 
166. export const instant: InstantConfig = true
167. ```
168. 
169. ## Version History
170. 
171. | Version   | Changes                                             |
172. | --------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
173. | `v16.x.x` | `instant` export introduced (Cache Components only) |
174.
````

</details>

2. title: prefetch
3. description: API reference for the prefetch route segment config.
4. related:
5.   title: Next Steps

10. ---
11. 
12. The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.
13. 
14. > **Good to know**:
15. >
16. > - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
17. > - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
18. > - The meaningful values to set are `'allow-runtime'`, `'partial'`, and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.
19. 
20. ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
21. export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'
22. 
23. export default function Page() {
24.   return <div>...</div>
25. }
26. ```
27. 
28. ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
29. export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'
30. 
31. export default function Page() {
32.   return <div>...</div>
33. }
34. ```
35. 
36. ## Options
37. 
38. ### `'allow-runtime'`
39. 
40. Allows Next.js to prefetch this segment at runtime. Today, setting this option causes Next.js to issue a runtime prefetch request, so the server can render a fresh response that includes runtime data like cookies, headers, and search params. Use this for personalized content when the latency and cost of runtime prefetching are appropriate for the segment.
41. 
42. > **Good to know**: When Next.js runtime-prefetches a segment, all downstream segments are included in the same runtime prefetch request. Segments deeper in the tree that are configured with `'force-disabled'` will still be prefetched as part of the runtime response.
43. 
44. ```tsx filename="page.tsx"
45. export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'
46. ```
47. 
48. ### `'partial'`
49. 
50. Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `<Link>` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link.
51. 
52. Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports.
53. 
54. ```tsx filename="page.tsx"
55. export const prefetch = 'partial'
56. ```
57. 
58. ### `'force-disabled'`
59. 
60. Never prefetch this segment. The client will not request segment data ahead of navigation. Use this for segments where prefetching would be wasteful, for example pages behind authentication that are rarely visited.
61. 
62. > **Good to know**: `'force-disabled'` does not prevent Next.js from prefetching metadata about the route. However, the actual segment data for this segment and all deeper segments will be omitted from prefetching.
63. 
64. ## Relationship with the `<Link prefetch>` prop
65. 
66. A prefetch starts with a `<Link>` that expresses intent (should this destination be prefetched, and how eagerly), and ends at a segment that sets a cost ceiling (how much work is it OK to do ahead of time, for any link that points here).
67. 
68. A destination can't know which links target it, so the segment config caps what any `<Link prefetch={true}>` pulls:
69. 
70. - [`'allow-runtime'`](#allow-runtime): App Shell plus runtime data (cookies, headers, search params).
71. - [`'partial'`](#partial): App Shell only.
72. - [`'force-disabled'`](#force-disabled): skip segment data entirely.
73. 
74. `<Link prefetch={false}>` skips prefetching at the link level regardless of how the destination is configured.
75. 
76. > **Good to know**: A prefetch may be served from a CDN cache, reuse a cached App Shell, or run a fresh server render. Wider prefetches lean toward fresh server work and cost more server CPU per page view.
77. 
78. ## TypeScript
79. 
80. ```tsx
81. type Prefetch = 'auto' | 'allow-runtime' | 'partial' | 'force-disabled'
82. 
83. export const prefetch: Prefetch = 'allow-runtime'
84. ```
85. 
86. ## Version History
87. 
88. | Version   | Changes                                              |
89. | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
90. | `v16.x.x` | `prefetch` export introduced (Cache Components only) |
91.
````

</details>

1. ---
2. title: 'use cache: private'
3. description: 'Learn how to use the "use cache: private" directive to cache functions that access runtime request APIs.'
4. related:
5.   title: Related
6.   description: View related API references.
7.   links:
8.     - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9.     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
10.     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
11.     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
12. ---
13. 
14. The `'use cache: private'` directive allows functions to access runtime request APIs like `cookies()`, `headers()`, and `searchParams` within a cached scope. However, results are **never stored on the server**, they're cached only in the browser's memory and do not persist across page reloads.
15. 
16. Reach for `'use cache: private'` when:
17. 
18. - You want to cache a function that already accesses runtime data, and refactoring to [move the runtime access outside and pass values as arguments](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#working-with-runtime-apis) is not practical.
19. - Compliance requirements prevent storing certain data on the server, even temporarily
20. 
21. Because this directive accesses runtime data, the function executes on every server render and is excluded from running during [static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) generation.
22. 
23. It is **not** possible to configure custom cache handlers for `'use cache: private'`.
24. 
25. For a comparison of the different cache directives, see [How `use cache: remote` differs from `use cache` and `use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote#how-use-cache-remote-differs-from-use-cache-and-use-cache-private).
26. 
27. ## Usage
28. 
29. To use `'use cache: private'`, enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in your `next.config.ts` file:
30. 
31. ```tsx filename="next.config.ts" switcher
32. import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
33. 
34. const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
35.   cacheComponents: true,
36. }
37. 
38. export default nextConfig
39. ```
40. 
41. ```jsx filename="next.config.js" switcher
42. /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
43. const nextConfig = {
44.   cacheComponents: true,
45. }
46. 
47. export default nextConfig
48. ```
49. 
50. Then add `'use cache: private'` to your function along with a `cacheLife` configuration.
51. 
52. > **Good to know**: This directive is not available in Route Handlers.
53. 
54. ### Basic example
55. 
56. In this example, we demonstrate that you can access cookies within a `'use cache: private'` scope:
57. 
58. ```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
59. import { Suspense } from 'react'
60. import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
61. import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
62. 
63. export async function generateStaticParams() {
64.   return [{ id: '1' }]
65. }
66. 
67. export default async function ProductPage({
68.   params,
69. }: {
70.   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
71. }) {
72.   const { id } = await params
73. 
74.   return (
75.     <div>
76.       <ProductDetails id={id} />
77.       <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading recommendations...</div>}>
78.         <Recommendations productId={id} />
79.       </Suspense>
80.     </div>
81.   )
82. }
83. 
84. async function Recommendations({ productId }: { productId: string }) {
85.   const recommendations = await getRecommendations(productId)
86. 
87.   return (
88.     <div>
89.       {recommendations.map((rec) => (
90.         <ProductCard key={rec.id} product={rec} />
91.       ))}
92.     </div>
93.   )
94. }
95. 
96. async function getRecommendations(productId: string) {
97.   'use cache: private'
98.   cacheTag(`recommendations-${productId}`)
99.   cacheLife({ stale: 60 })
100. 
101.   // Access cookies within private cache functions
102.   const sessionId = (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'guest'
103. 
104.   return getPersonalizedRecommendations(productId, sessionId)
105. }
106. ```
107. 
108. ```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher
109. import { Suspense } from 'react'
110. import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
111. import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
112. 
113. export async function generateStaticParams() {
114.   return [{ id: '1' }]
115. }
116. 
117. export default async function ProductPage({ params }) {
118.   const { id } = await params
119. 
120.   return (
121.     <div>
122.       <ProductDetails id={id} />
123.       <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading recommendations...</div>}>
124.         <Recommendations productId={id} />
125.       </Suspense>
126.     </div>
127.   )
128. }
129. 
130. async function Recommendations({ productId }) {
131.   const recommendations = await getRecommendations(productId)
132. 
133.   return (
134.     <div>
135.       {recommendations.map((rec) => (
136.         <ProductCard key={rec.id} product={rec} />
137.       ))}
138.     </div>
139.   )
140. }
141. 
142. async function getRecommendations(productId) {
143.   'use cache: private'
144.   cacheTag(`recommendations-${productId}`)
145.   cacheLife({ stale: 60 })
146. 
147.   // Access cookies within private cache functions
148.   const sessionId = (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'guest'
149. 
150.   return getPersonalizedRecommendations(productId, sessionId)
151. }
152. ```
153. 
154. > **Good to know**: The `stale` time must be at least 30 seconds for runtime prefetching to work. See [`cacheLife` client cache behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#client-cache-behavior) for details.
155. 
156. ## Request APIs allowed in private caches
157. 
158. The following request-specific APIs can be used inside `'use cache: private'` functions:
159. 
160. | API            | Allowed in `use cache` | Allowed in `'use cache: private'` |
161. | -------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
162. | `cookies()`    | No                     | Yes                               |
163. | `headers()`    | No                     | Yes                               |
164. | `searchParams` | No                     | Yes                               |
165. | `connection()` | No                     | No                                |
166. 
167. > **Note:** The [`connection()`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) API is prohibited in both `use cache` and `'use cache: private'` as it provides connection-specific information that cannot be safely cached.
168. 
169. ## Version History
170. 
171. | Version   | Changes                                                              |
172. | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
173. | `v16.0.0` | `"use cache: private"` is enabled with the Cache Components feature. |
174.
````

</details>

50.       } else {
51.         granularity = meta.granularity ?? "1digit";
52.       }
53.     } catch (error) {
54.       console.error("Failed to fetch area metadata:", error);
55.     }
56.   }
57. 
58.   return {
59.     title: `KRAUSS Gebietsmanagement - ${granularity.toUpperCase()} PLZ`,
60.     description: `Interaktives Gebietsmanagement für deutsche Postleitzahlen mit ${granularity} Granularität`,
61.     openGraph: {
62.       title: `KRAUSS Gebietsmanagement - ${granularity.toUpperCase()} PLZ`,
63.       description: `Interaktives Gebietsmanagement für deutsche Postleitzahlen mit ${granularity} Granularität`,
64.       type: "website",
65.     },
66.   };
67. }
68. 
69. export default async function PostalCodesPage({
70.   params,
71.   searchParams,
72. }: PostalCodesPageProps) {
73.   const { areaId: areaIdParam } = await params;
74. 
75.   const areaId = parseInt(areaIdParam, 10);
76. 
77.   // Guard against NaN areaId (can happen during redirect race conditions)
78.   if (Number.isNaN(areaId) || areaId <= 0) {
79.     return (
80.       <>
81.         <SiteHeader />
82.         <div className="h-full" data-layout="fullscreen">
83.           <PostalCodesViewSkeleton />
84.         </div>
85.       </>
86.     );
87.   }
88. 
89.   // Get area meta using only static params — no searchParams access here.
90.   // This allows the static PPR shell (header + skeleton) to be prerendered.
91.   // versionId is resolved inside ServerPostalCodesView (inside Suspense).
92.   let granularity = "1digit";
93.   let country: CountryCode = DEFAULT_COUNTRY;
94.   let areaName: string | null = null;
95.   try {
96.     const meta = await getAreaMeta(areaId);
97.     granularity = meta.granularity ?? "1digit";
98.     country =
99.       meta.country && isValidCountryCode(meta.country)
100.         ? meta.country
101.         : DEFAULT_COUNTRY;
102.     areaName = meta.name;
103.   } catch (error) {
104.     console.error("Failed to fetch area metadata:", error);
105.   }
106. 
107.   return (
108.     <>
109.       {/* Preload map data APIs so fetches start during HTML streaming */}
110.       <link
111.         rel="preload"
112.         href="/api/states"
113.         as="fetch"
114.         crossOrigin="anonymous"
115.       />
116.       <link
117.         rel="preload"
118.         href="/api/countries"
119.         as="fetch"
120.         crossOrigin="anonymous"
121.       />
122.       <SiteHeader title={areaName ?? "Gebietsmanagement"}>
123.         <Suspense fallback={<VersionIndicatorSkeleton />}>
124.           <VersionIndicator areaId={areaId} />
125.         </Suspense>
126.       </SiteHeader>
127.       <div className="h-full" data-layout="fullscreen">
128.         <PostalCodesErrorBoundary>
129.           <Suspense fallback={<PostalCodesViewSkeleton />}>
130.             <ServerPostalCodesView
131.               defaultGranularity={granularity}
132.               country={country}
133.               areaId={areaId}
134.               searchParamsPromise={searchParams}
135.             />
136.           </Suspense>
137.         </PostalCodesErrorBoundary>
138.       </div>
139.     </>
140.   );
141. }
142.
```

1. ---
2. title: Ensuring instant navigations
3. description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.
4. nav_title: Instant navigation
5. related:
6.   title: Learn more
7.   description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation.
8.   links:
9.     - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
10.     - app/guides/runtime-prefetching
11.     - app/getting-started/caching
12.     - app/getting-started/revalidating
13.     - app/guides/prefetching
14. ---
15. 
16. This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
17. 
18. ## What "instant" means
19. 
20. A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21. 
22. > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23. 
24. A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25. 
26. Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27. 
28. <details>
29. <summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30. 
31. On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32. 
33. On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
34. 
35. This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
36. 
37. </details>
38. 
39. Runtime prefetching extends the static shell with request-specific content like the user's name from a cookie, by invoking the route at prefetch time. Ensuring navigations are instant is the foundation: a route that doesn't navigate instantly without runtime prefetching won't navigate instantly with it either. See [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) for the patterns.
40. 
41. ## The tools
42. 
43. ### Build the static shell
44. 
45. With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
46. 
47. > **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the runtime prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
48. 
49. **`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
50. 
51. > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. With [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), the information is available and such a fallback becomes part of the instant UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
52. 
53. Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route: a fallback that renders instantly during client navigations when nothing else is ready. See [App Shells](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#app-shells) for how to enable them and how they pair with runtime prefetching.
54. 
55. ### Tune what `<Link>` prefetches
56. 
57. Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `<Link>` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. The shell is shared across every link to the same route, so rendering a `<Link>` is effectively free.
58. 
59. To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
60. 
61. ```tsx
62. <Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
63.   Checkout
64. </Link>
65. ```
66. 
67. To prefetch with the user's session (cookies, headers, the full URL), opt the destination segment into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) with `export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'`.
68. 
69. ### Validate instant navigation
70. 
71. By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
72. 
73. To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
74. 
75. ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4-8}
76. import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
77. 
78. const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
79.   cacheComponents: true,
80.   experimental: {
81.     instantInsights: {
82.       validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
83.     },
84.   },
85. }
86. 
87. export default nextConfig
88. ```
89. 
90. <details>
91. <summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
92. 
93. For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
94. 
95. For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
96. 
97. - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
98. - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
99. 
100. Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
101. 
102. </details>
103. 
104. ### Test it in CI
105. 
106. The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern.
107. 
108. ### Inspect loading states
109. 
110. The **Navigation Inspector** in the Next.js DevTools freezes the page at its initial loading state, showing the static shell on direct visits and the prefetched destination on client navigations. Use the inspector to see how much meaningful content lands in the shell.
111. 
112. Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. See [Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) for the workflow.
113. 
114. See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell) for patterns to reduce fallback coverage and pull more content into the shell.
115. 
116. ## A page that navigates instantly
117. 
118. To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The goal is that navigating to and between products is instant.
119. 
120. The product page fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory.
121. 
122. - There is no `generateStaticParams`, meaning `slug` is only known at request time
123. - Both components await `params` to get the `slug`, which suspends. Each has its own `<Suspense>` boundary
124. - **Product info** rarely changes and is queried from the db using a cached function
125. - **Inventory** must be fresh on each request. The db query is inside a `<Suspense>` boundary
126. 
127. ```tsx filename="app/store/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={7-12,30-32}
128. import { Suspense } from 'react'
129. import { db } from '@/lib/db'
130. 
131. export default function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/store/[slug]'>) {
132.   return (
133.     <div>
134.       <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading product...</p>}>
135.         <ProductInfo params={props.params} />
136.       </Suspense>
137.       <Suspense fallback={<p>Checking availability...</p>}>
138.         <Inventory params={props.params} />
139.       </Suspense>
140.     </div>
141.   )
142. }
143. 
144. type Params = PageProps<'/store/[slug]'>['params']
145. 
146. async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Params }) {
147.   const { slug } = await params
148.   const product = await getProduct(slug)
149.   return (
150.     <>
151.       <h1>{product.name}</h1>
152.       <p>${product.price}</p>
153.     </>
154.   )
155. }
156. 
157. async function getProduct(slug: string) {
158.   'use cache'
159.   return db.products.findBySlug(slug)
160. }
161. 
162. async function Inventory({ params }: { params: Params }) {
163.   const { slug } = await params
164.   const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug)
165.   return <p>{item.count} in stock</p>
166. }
167. ```
168. 
169. Cache Components validates this route automatically in development. If something would block a navigation, the dev overlay surfaces a **blocking-route** insight that names the offending component and points at these fixes:
170. 
171. <FixCardGrid>
172.   <FixCard
173.     group="cache"
174.     title="Cache the component or data"
175.     href="/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic#cache-the-component-or-data"
176.     snippets={[
177.       { text: 'async function Posts() {' },
178.       { text: '  "use cache"', highlight: true },
179.       { text: '  return <List items={…} />' },
180.       { text: '}' },
181.     ]}
182.   />
183.   <FixCard
184.     group="stream"
185.     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
186.     href="/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"
187.     snippets={[
188.       { text: '<Suspense fallback={…}>', highlight: true },
189.       { text: '  <DataChild />' },
190.       { text: '</Suspense>', highlight: true },
191.     ]}
192.   />
193. </FixCardGrid>
194. 
195. > **Good to know:** Each fix card links to a detailed walkthrough with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs. Click a card to dive in.
196. 
197. Validation runs on every page load using the real request from your browser, so dynamic params like `[slug]` are checked against actual values as you navigate.
198. 
199. ## Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools
200. 
201. As you develop a route, the Next.js DevTools let you see what your users see on page loads and client navigations before dynamic data streams in. Use it to verify that your loading states look right, confirm the content you expect appears immediately, and iterate on where to place `<Suspense>` boundaries.
202. 
203. The [React DevTools Suspense panel](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) complements this: it lists the `<Suspense>` boundaries in the tree and lets you toggle each one between its fallback and resolved state, so you can see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page.
204. 
205. {/* TODO: screenshot — React DevTools Suspense panel listing boundaries with toggle controls */}
206. 
207. The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled:
208. 
209. ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4}
210. import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
211. 
212. const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
213.   cacheComponents: true,
214. }
215. 
216. export default nextConfig
217. ```
218. 
219. Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then toggle **Pause on navigations**. The panel shows **Awaiting navigation...** While the toggle is on:
220. 
````

A "Cache disabled" variant appears when caches are bypassed. Reload once caches are warm to see a production-representative view.

236. > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. Client-side hooks like `useSearchParams` suspend on page loads (search params are not known at build time) but resolve synchronously on client navigations (the router already has the params).
237. 
238. ## Prevent regressions with e2e tests
239. 
240. Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship.
241. 
242. The `@next/playwright` package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`:
243. 
244. ```bash package="pnpm"
245. pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
246. ```
247. 
248. ```bash package="npm"
249. npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
250. ```
251. 
252. ```bash package="yarn"
253. yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
254. ```
255. 
256. ```bash package="bun"
257. bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
258. ```
259. 
260. Then use it in a test:
261. 
262. ```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts"
263. import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'
264. import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
265. 
266. test('product title appears instantly', async ({ page }) => {
267.   await page.goto('/store/shoes')
268. 
269.   await instant(page, async () => {
270.     await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]')
271.     await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
272.   })
273. 
274.   // After instant() exits, dynamic content streams in
275.   await expect(page.locator('text=in stock')).toBeVisible()
276. })
277. ```
278. 
279. Inside the `instant()` callback, only the static shell is visible. After the callback finishes, dynamic content streams in and you can assert on the full page.
280. 
281. Focus these tests on the user flows that matter most. Run them against your dev server during development, and in CI against your build output so regressions fail the pipeline.
282. 
283. ## Fixing a navigation that blocks
284. 
285. Consider a different route, `/shop/[slug]`, with the same data requirements as `/store/[slug]` but implemented without local `<Suspense>` boundaries or caching:
286. 
287. ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx"
288. import { db } from '@/lib/db'
289. 
290. export default async function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) {
291.   const { slug } = await props.params
292.   const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug)
293.   const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug)
294.   return (
295.     <div>
296.       <h1>{product.name}</h1>
297.       <p>${product.price}</p>
298.       <p>{item.count} in stock</p>
299.     </div>
300.   )
301. }
302. ```
303. 
304. The root layout wraps `{children}` in a `<Suspense>` boundary:
305. 
306. ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={9}
307. export default function RootLayout({
308.   children,
309. }: {
310.   children: React.ReactNode
311. }) {
312.   return (
313.     <html lang="en">
314.       <body>
315.         <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading...</p>}>{children}</Suspense>
316.       </body>
317.     </html>
318.   )
319. }
320. ```
321. 
322. On an initial page load, the root `<Suspense>` catches the async work and streams the page in behind the fallback.
323. 
324. Everything appears to work. But on a client navigation from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`, the shared layout is `/shop` and only the content below it re-renders. The root `<Suspense>` boundary is above that layout and is not triggered for this navigation. The page fetches uncached data with no local `<Suspense>` boundary, blocking the navigation until the server finishes rendering.
325. 
326. You can see this with the DevTools. Try a **page load**: the root `<Suspense>` catches everything and **"Loading..."** appears. Now try a **client navigation** between two `/shop/` pages: there is no fallback UI to show for the destination because no `<Suspense>` boundary sits below the shared layout. The navigation blocks until the server completes. Navigations from other routes into `/shop/` also block.
327. 
328. ### Step 1: See what validation catches
329. 
330. Cache Components simulates navigations at every shared layout boundary in this route. The page awaits `params` and accesses uncached data at the top level, with no `<Suspense>` boundary around any of it. The first thing validation catches is the `await params` at the top level.
331. 
332. {/* TODO: screenshot — Next.js dev overlay surfacing the blocking-route insight on the broken /shop/[slug] route, with the await params at the top level highlighted */}
333. 
334. ### Step 2: Fix the validation error
335. 
336. There is no `generateStaticParams` here, `slug` is only known at request time. Because awaiting `params` suspends, the page component can't do it at the top level. Instead, move the `await params` into separate components, pass `params` to each, and wrap them with `<Suspense>`.
337. 
338. For each component, decide:
339. 
340. **Product details** (name, price) rarely change. Cache the data function with `use cache`:
341. 
342. ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx"
343. async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) {
344.   const { slug } = await params
345.   const product = await getProduct(slug)
346.   return (
347.     <>
348.       <h1>{product.name}</h1>
349.       <p>${product.price}</p>
350.     </>
351.   )
352. }
353. 
354. async function getProduct(slug: string) {
355.   'use cache'
356.   return db.products.findBySlug(slug)
357. }
358. ```
359. 
360. > **Good to know:** In serverless deployments, in-memory caching with `"use cache"` will not persist across instances. Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching.
361. 
362. **Inventory** must be fresh each request. Leave it uncached:
363. 
364. ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx"
365. async function Inventory({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) {
366.   const { slug } = await params
367.   const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug)
368.   return <p>{item.count} in stock</p>
369. }
370. ```
371. 
372. The page passes `params` to each component and wraps them with `<Suspense>`:
373. 
374. ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={7-12}
375. import { Suspense } from 'react'
376. import { db } from '@/lib/db'
377. 
378. export default function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) {
379.   return (
380.     <div>
381.       <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading product...</p>}>
382.         <ProductInfo params={props.params} />
383.       </Suspense>
384.       <Suspense fallback={<p>Checking availability...</p>}>
385.         <Inventory params={props.params} />
386.       </Suspense>
387.     </div>
388.   )
389. }
390. ```
391. 
392. Validation passes. Open the DevTools and try a client navigation. The product name and price appear immediately, and **"Checking availability..."** shows where inventory will stream in.
393. 
394. ### Iterate on loading states
395. 
396. {/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */}
397. 
398. Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `<Suspense>` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation.
399. 
400. The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time.
401. 
402. Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent.
403. 
404. ## AI workflow
405. 
406. The observe-fix-iterate loop is well suited to AI coding agents:
407. 
408. - **Observe**: read validation insights in the dev overlay and dev server console.
409. - **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or `<Suspense>`). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation, whether that's in dev or a build.
410. - **Iterate**: run an `instant()` test to check what appears in the shell. Because the output is deterministic, the agent can assert on it without flaky retries.
411. 
412. The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model. It follows the insights and errors until they're gone.
413. 
414. For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down. You can hint at what data needs to be fresh on load and what can be cached, and the agent will move the `<Suspense>` and `use cache` placement accordingly.
415. 
416. Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers:
417. 
418. - **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell.
419. - **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile.
420. - **Runtime prefetching** (nav-only): when I/O depends on `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`, opt the route into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) so the framework prerenders it at link-prefetch time.
421. 
422. Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect.
423. 
424. For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). It exposes the Next.js DevTools (including PPR shells) as shell commands agents can read and drive, so the loop becomes: make a change, snapshot the shell, check what's in it, adjust.
425. 
426. {/* TODO: distribution of the skill/plugin */}
427. The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-optimizer) skill packages this loop: shared preflight, the three levers, plan-mode gating, before/after capture verify, and a no-shell bailout when the route is fully blocking. It picks between two sub-loops based on the request: page-render (grow the static shell of a single page) or in-app navigation (capture the destination's suspended boundaries after a click).
428. 
429. ## Opting out
430. 
431. Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes.
432. 
433. The dev overlay surfaces this as the **Block** fix alongside every insight:
434. 
435. <FixCardGrid>
436.   <FixCard
437.     group="block"
438.     title="Allow blocking route"
439.     href="/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic#allow-blocking-route"
440.     snippets={[
441.       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
442.       { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
443.     ]}
444.   />
445. </FixCardGrid>
446. 
447. Set `instant = false` on the page or layout file. This opts the segment out of validation feedback. The segment may still navigate instantly if its structure supports it; the framework just won't surface insights for it. Navigations between sibling segments below are still validated.
448. 
449. ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
450. export const instant = false
451. ```
452. 
453. With `false` on `/dashboard/layout.tsx`, validation no longer flags navigations into `/dashboard` from outside; navigations between `/dashboard/a` and `/dashboard/b` are still checked.
454. 
455. For opted-out segments, the navigation blocks on the server. If the content depends on cookies or headers but has a known cache lifetime, [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) can prerender it ahead of click instead of opting out.
456. 
457. ## Next steps
458. 
459. - [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the recommended `<Link>` defaults and the migration path off `unstable_eager`
460. - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for the full configuration
461. - [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) when parts of your route depend on cookies or headers and you want those in the shell
462. - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering
463. - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag`
464. 
465. {/* Ensure we include instant navs skill learnings: see https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/94152 */}
466.
````

1. import { Suspense } from "react";
2. 
3. import { PostalCodesErrorBoundary } from "@/components/ui/error-boundaries";
4. import { PostalCodesViewSkeleton } from "@/components/ui/loading-skeletons";
5. import type { CountryCode } from "@/lib/config/countries";
6. import { DEFAULT_COUNTRY } from "@/lib/config/countries";
7. import {
8.   getAreaMeta,
9.   getLayers,
10.   getVersionSummaries,
11.   getChangeSummaries,
12.   getUndoRedoStatus,
13.   getAreaTags,
14. } from "@/lib/db/data-functions";
15. 
16. import { PostalCodesViewClientWithLayers } from "./postal-codes-view-client-layers";
17. 
18. interface ServerPostalCodesViewProps {
19.   defaultGranularity: string;
20.   country?: CountryCode;
21.   areaId: number;
22.   searchParamsPromise: Promise<Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>>;
23. }
24. 
25. export default async function ServerPostalCodesView({
26.   defaultGranularity,
27.   country = DEFAULT_COUNTRY,
28.   areaId,
29.   searchParamsPromise,
30. }: ServerPostalCodesViewProps) {
31.   // Guard against NaN areaId (can happen during redirect race conditions)
32.   if (!areaId || Number.isNaN(areaId)) {
33.     return <PostalCodesViewSkeleton />;
34.   }
35. 
36.   // Resolve versionId from searchParams here (inside Suspense boundary).
37.   // This keeps the page's static shell free of dynamic searchParams access.
38.   const searchParams = await searchParamsPromise;
39.   const versionIdRaw = Array.isArray(searchParams.versionId)
40.     ? searchParams.versionId[0]
41.     : searchParams.versionId;
42.   const versionId = versionIdRaw ? parseInt(versionIdRaw, 10) : null;
43. 
44.   // Server Component: initiate all fetches as promises
45.   // Geodata (postal codes) is now fetched client-side via API route
46.   // to avoid serializing ~9.6MB of GeoJSON into the RSC payload
47.   // States data also fetched client-side to avoid 246KB RSC payload bloat
48.   // getAreaMeta is already called by page.tsx — this hits the same "use cache"
49.   // entry (same function + same areaId arg), avoiding extra DB queries
50.   const areaMetaPromise = getAreaMeta(areaId);
51.   const areaTagsPromise = getAreaTags(areaId);
52.   const layersPromise = getLayers(areaId);
53.   const versionsPromise = getVersionSummaries(areaId);
54.   const changesPromise = getChangeSummaries(areaId, { limit: 50 });
55.   const undoRedoStatusPromise = getUndoRedoStatus(areaId);
56. 
57.   return (
58.     <PostalCodesErrorBoundary>
59.       <Suspense fallback={<PostalCodesViewSkeleton />}>
60.         <PostalCodesViewClientWithLayers
61.           defaultGranularity={defaultGranularity}
62.           country={country}
63.           areaId={areaId}
64.           areaMetaPromise={areaMetaPromise}
65.           areaTagsPromise={areaTagsPromise}
66.           layersPromise={layersPromise}
67.           undoRedoStatusPromise={undoRedoStatusPromise}
68.           isViewingVersion={versionId !== null && versionId > 0}
69.           versionId={versionId}
70.           versionsPromise={versionsPromise}
71.           changesPromise={changesPromise}
72.         />
73.       </Suspense>
74.     </PostalCodesErrorBoundary>
75.   );
76. }
77.

471.       (layerId: number) => {
472.         const data = dataRef.current;
473.         if (!data) return;
474.         const layer = optimisticLayersRef.current.find((l) => l.id === layerId);
475.         if (!layer?.postalCodes?.length) return;
476. 
477.         const codeSet = new Set(layer.postalCodes.map((pc) => pc.postalCode));
478.         let minLng = Infinity,
479.           maxLng = -Infinity,
480.           minLat = Infinity,
481.           maxLat = -Infinity;
482.         let found = false;
483. 
484.         for (const feature of data.features) {
485.           if (!codeSet.has(feature.properties?.code)) continue;
486.           found = true;
487.           const coords: number[][] = [];
488.           const geom = feature.geometry;
489.           if (geom.type === "Polygon") {
490.             for (const ring of geom.coordinates)
491.               for (const c of ring) coords.push(c);
492.           } else if (geom.type === "MultiPolygon") {
493.             for (const poly of geom.coordinates)
494.               for (const ring of poly) for (const c of ring) coords.push(c);
495.           }
496.           for (const [lng, lat] of coords) {
497.             if (lng < minLng) minLng = lng;
498.             if (lng > maxLng) maxLng = lng;
499.             if (lat < minLat) minLat = lat;
500.             if (lat > maxLat) maxLat = lat;
501.           }
502.         }
503. 
504.         if (!found) return;
505. 
506.         const centerLng = (minLng + maxLng) / 2;
507.         const centerLat = (minLat + maxLat) / 2;
508.         // Approximate zoom: wider bbox → lower zoom
509.         const lngSpan = maxLng - minLng;
510.         const latSpan = maxLat - minLat;
511.         const span = Math.max(lngSpan, latSpan);
512.         const zoom = Math.max(
513.           5,
514.           Math.min(13, Math.round(Math.log2(360 / span)) - 1)
515.         );
516. 
517.         setMapCenterZoom([centerLng, centerLat], zoom);
518.       },
519.       [setMapCenterZoom]
520.     );

169. class MapRecoveryBoundary extends Component<
170.   { children: ReactNode },
171.   { hasError: boolean }
172. > {
173.   constructor(props: { children: ReactNode }) {
174.     super(props);
175.     this.state = { hasError: false };

182.   componentDidCatch(error: Error, _info: ErrorInfo) {
183.     // Only auto-recover from known map destruction errors
184.     const isMapDestroyedError =
185.       error.message?.includes("_loaded") ||
186.       error.message?.includes("getProjection") ||
187.       error.message?.includes("getSource") ||
188.       error.message?.includes("getLayer") ||
189.       error.message?.includes("getStyle");
190.     if (isMapDestroyedError) {
191.       // Schedule reset on next frame — the new render will create a fresh map
192.       requestAnimationFrame(() => {
193.         this.setState({ hasError: false });
194.       });
195.     }
196.   }

199.     if (this.state.hasError) {
200.       // Return minimal placeholder during the single-frame recovery
201.       return <div className="w-full h-full" />;
202.     }
203.     return this.props.children;
204.   }
205. }

310.   data,
311.   featureIndex,
312.   country,

314.   data: FeatureCollection<Polygon | MultiPolygon>;
315.   featureIndex?: Map<string, Feature<Polygon | MultiPolygon>[]>;

323.   const handleSearch = useCallback(
324.     (e: React.FormEvent) => {
325.       e.preventDefault();
326.       const code = query.trim();
327.       if (!code || !mapRef) return;
328.       const key = resolveFeatureKey(code, country, featureIndex);
329.       const features = featureIndex?.get(key) ?? featureIndex?.get(code);
330.       if (!features || features.length === 0) return;
331.       // Compute bounding box of first feature
332.       const allCoords: number[][] = [];
333.       for (const ft of features) {
334.         const geom = ft.geometry;
335.         if (geom.type === "Polygon") {
336.           for (const ring of geom.coordinates) {
337.             for (const c of ring) allCoords.push(c);
338.           }
339.         } else if (geom.type === "MultiPolygon") {
340.           for (const poly of geom.coordinates) {
341.             for (const ring of poly) {
342.               for (const c of ring) allCoords.push(c);
343.             }
344.           }
345.         }
346.       }
347.       if (allCoords.length === 0) return;
348.       const lngs = allCoords.map((c) => c[0]);
349.       const lats = allCoords.map((c) => c[1]);
350.       const minLng = Math.min(...lngs);
351.       const maxLng = Math.max(...lngs);
352.       const minLat = Math.min(...lats);
353.       const maxLat = Math.max(...lats);
354.       mapRef.fitBounds(
355.         [
356.           [minLng, minLat],
357.           [maxLng, maxLat],
358.         ],
359.         { padding: 80, duration: 800 }
360.       );
361.       setOpen(false);
362.       setQuery("");
363.     },
364.     [query, mapRef, featureIndex, country]
365.   );

1. import { useQueryState } from "nuqs";

4. import { DACH_CENTER, DACH_ZOOM } from "../config/countries";

7. const DEFAULT_CENTER = DACH_CENTER;
8. const DEFAULT_ZOOM = DACH_ZOOM;
9. 
10. function parseMapViewFromSearch(search: string) {
11.   const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
12.   const raw = params.get("mapView");
13.   if (!raw)
14.     return { center: DEFAULT_CENTER as [number, number], zoom: DEFAULT_ZOOM };
15.   try {
16.     return JSON.parse(raw) as { center: [number, number]; zoom: number };
17.   } catch {
18.     return { center: DEFAULT_CENTER as [number, number], zoom: DEFAULT_ZOOM };
19.   }
20. }
21. 
22. // Reads mapView directly from window.location — bypasses nuqs to prevent
23. // the full Router cascade that fires on every replaceState during map pan.
24. // Only subscribes to popstate (back/forward navigation), not pan/zoom writes.
25. export function useMapView() {
26.   const [, forceUpdate] = useReducer((x: number) => x + 1, 0);
27. 
28.   useEffect(() => {
29.     window.addEventListener("popstate", forceUpdate);
30.     return () => window.removeEventListener("popstate", forceUpdate);
31.   }, []);
32. 
33.   const parsed = parseMapViewFromSearch(
34.     typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.location.search : ""
35.   );
36. 
37.   const parsedLng = parsed.center[0];
38.   const parsedLat = parsed.center[1];
39. 
40.   const prevCenterRef = useRef<[number, number]>([parsedLng, parsedLat]);
41.   const stableCenter = useMemo(() => {
42.     const [prevLng, prevLat] = prevCenterRef.current;
43.     if (parsedLng === prevLng && parsedLat === prevLat) {
44.       return prevCenterRef.current;
45.     }
46.     const next: [number, number] = [parsedLng, parsedLat];
47.     prevCenterRef.current = next;
48.     return next;
49.   }, [parsedLng, parsedLat]);
50. 
51.   const setMapView = useStableCallback(
52.     (view: { center: [number, number]; zoom: number }) => {
53.       const url = new URL(window.location.href);
54.       url.searchParams.set("mapView", JSON.stringify(view));
55.       // "__nuqs__" marker tells nuqs's history patch to skip sync — prevents
56.       // all nuqs consumers from re-rendering on every map pan/zoom write.
57.       window.history.replaceState(
58.         window.history.state,
59.         "__nuqs__",
60.         url.toString()
61.       );
62.     }
63.   );
64. 
65.   return [{ center: stableCenter, zoom: parsed.zoom }, setMapView] as const;
66. }

1. "use client";
2. 
3. import { IconMapPin, IconSearch, IconX } from "@tabler/icons-react";
4. import Link from "next/link";
5. import { useCallback, useState, useTransition } from "react";
6. import { useEffect } from "react";
7. import { useDebounce } from "use-debounce";
8. 
9. import {
10.   searchPostalCodeInAreasAction,
11.   type PlzSearchResult,
12. } from "@/app/actions/area-actions";
13. import { SidebarInput } from "@/components/ui/sidebar";
14. 
15. export function PlzSearch() {
16.   const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
17.   const [results, setResults] = useState<PlzSearchResult[]>([]);
18.   const [notFound, setNotFound] = useState(false);
19.   const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();
20.   const [debouncedQuery] = useDebounce(query, 350);
21. 
22.   useEffect(() => {
23.     const code = debouncedQuery.trim();
24.     if (code.length < 2) {
25.       setResults([]);
26.       setNotFound(false);
27.       return;
28.     }
29.     startTransition(async () => {
30.       const res = await searchPostalCodeInAreasAction(code);
31.       if (res.success) {
32.         setResults(res.data ?? []);
33.         setNotFound((res.data ?? []).length === 0);
34.       }
35.     });
36.   }, [debouncedQuery]);
37. 
38.   const handleClear = useCallback(() => {
39.     setQuery("");
40.     setResults([]);
41.     setNotFound(false);
42.   }, []);
43. 
44.   return (
45.     <div className="relative px-2 pb-1">
46.       <div className="relative">
47.         <IconSearch className="absolute left-2.5 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 h-3.5 w-3.5 text-muted-foreground pointer-events-none" />
48.         <SidebarInput
49.           value={query}
50.           onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
51.           placeholder="PLZ suchen…"
52.           className="pl-8 pr-7 h-8 text-xs"
53.         />
54.         {query && (
55.           <button
56.             type="button"
57.             onClick={handleClear}
58.             className="absolute right-2 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground"
59.           >
60.             <IconX className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
61.           </button>
62.         )}
63.       </div>
64. 
65.       {(results.length > 0 || notFound) && (
66.         <div className="mt-1 rounded-md border bg-popover shadow-sm text-xs overflow-hidden">
67.           {notFound && !isPending && (
68.             <div className="px-3 py-2 text-muted-foreground">
69.               Nicht gefunden
70.             </div>
71.           )}
72.           {results.map((r) => (
73.             <Link
74.               key={`${r.areaId}-${r.layerId}`}
75.               href={`/postal-codes/${r.areaId}`}
76.               onClick={handleClear}
77.               className="flex items-start gap-2 px-3 py-2 hover:bg-accent transition-colors"
78.             >
79.               <span
80.                 className="mt-0.5 h-2.5 w-2.5 rounded-full shrink-0"
81.                 style={{ backgroundColor: r.layerColor }}
82.               />
83.               <div className="min-w-0">
84.                 <div className="font-medium truncate">{r.areaName}</div>
85.                 <div className="text-muted-foreground truncate flex items-center gap-1">
86.                   <IconMapPin className="h-3 w-3 shrink-0" />
87.                   {r.layerName}
88.                 </div>
89.               </div>
90.             </Link>
91.           ))}
92.         </div>
93.       )}
94.     </div>
95.   );
96. }
97.
